name: Question 3
problem:
For the function

$$
G(s)=\frac{1}{s({s}^{2}+36)},\,s>0
$$

find the inverse Laplace transform of $G(s),$ given that
$L{\operatorname{sin}⁡(\omega t)}=\frac{\omega }{{s}^{2}+{\omega }^{2}}.$
worked_solution:
Notice that we can write $G(s)$ as 

$$
G(s)=\frac{1}{s({s}^{2}+36)}=\frac{F(s)}{s},
$$

where $F(s)=\frac{1}{{s}^{2}+36}.$
Also, we know that

$$
L{\operatorname{sin}⁡(\omega t)}=\frac{\omega }{{s}^{2}+{\omega }^{2}}.
$$

Thus, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{L}^{-1}{F(s)} & ={L}^{-1}\,{\frac{1}{{s}^{2}+36}} \\  & ={L}^{-1}\,{\frac{1}{6}\cdot \frac{6}{{s}^{2}+36}} \\  & =\frac{1}{6}\,{L}^{-1}\,{\frac{6}{{s}^{2}+{6}^{2}}} \\  & =\frac{1}{6}\,sin\,(6t).\end{aligned}
$$

Additionally, we know that if $L{f(t)}=F(s)$, then

$$
L{{\int }_{0}^{t}f(τ)\,\text{d}τ}=\frac{F(s)}{s}.
$$

Using the property above in reverse, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{L}^{-1}{G(s)} & ={L}^{-1}{\frac{F(s)}{s}} \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{t}f(τ)\,\text{d}τ \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{t}\frac{1}{6}\,sin\,(6τ)\,\text{d}τ \\  & =-\frac{1}{36}cos\,(6τ)\,{|}_{0}^{t} \\  & =\frac{1}{36}(1-cos\,(6t)).\end{aligned}
$$

Question 3
?

For the function G(s)=1s(s2+36),s>0 find the inverse Laplace transform of G(s), given that L{sin⁡(ωt)}=ωs2+ω2.

a
136(1−cos(6t))
b
16sin(6t)
c
136(1−cos⁡(36t))
d
136(1−sin(6t))
e
136cos(6t)
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

Notice that we can write G(s) as G(s)=1s(s2+36)=F(s)s, where F(s)=1s2+36. Also, we know that L{sin⁡(ωt)}=ωs2+ω2. Thus, we get L−1{F(s)}=L−1{1s2+36}=L−1{16⋅6s2+36}=16L−1{6s2+62}=16sin(6t).

Additionally, we know that if L{f(t)}=F(s), then L{∫0tf(τ)dτ}=F(s)s.

Using the property above in reverse, we obtain L−1{G(s)}=L−1{F(s)s}=∫0tf(τ)dτ=∫0t16sin(6τ)dτ=−136cos(6τ)|0t=136(1−cos(6t)).
